verdicts.message: Duplicated block (10 lines × 2 locations): src/http/routes/catalog-routes.ts:15 · src/http/routes/catalog-routes.ts:36 — all 2 copies are in the same file, and the CITED SPAN is not a self-contained block — it runs from inside one construct into the next (the tail of a branch plus the head of the following one, a run of switch arms, the end of a declaration plus the list that follows it) rather than covering a whole unit. So do not lift these lines literally: no call can be substituted for a half-open construct. Extract the enclosing repeated UNIT instead — the whole function, component or branch these lines sit in — and where the repetition IS the construct (a run of switch arms, a stack of near-identical declarations) replace it with one table or registry looked up by key rather than a helper each arm calls. The copies still drift apart the first time only one of them is edited, which is why this is reported.

verdicts.message: Duplicated block with local edits (7 matched lines × 2 locations): src/http/problem.ts:24 · src/http/problem.ts:32 — the two spans are one implementation copied and then locally edited — 59 tokens are still identical, in the same order in both spans, with only local edits between them. The copies have already begun to drift, which is this row's finding: an edit made to one and not the other changes behaviour silently. Diff the two spans first to learn what genuinely differs, then extract the shared core into one module both sites use, passing the differences in as parameters — or, if one copy exists only because the other could not be imported from its context, make one of them the single source the other is generated or re-exported from. If one copy is no longer reachable, delete it rather than letting it shadow the live one.

verdicts.message: No named authorization policies: Authorization IS enforced here (by route guards, auth middleware or checks that refuse a caller) — this is NOT a claim that endpoints are unprotected. What's missing is a NAMED rule set: who may do what is encoded inline where it is checked, so the rules can't be listed, reviewed or tested apart from the code that applies them. Recommendation, not a defect.
verdicts.reason: Disproof: src/http/scopes.ts names the three scopes and every /api route declares its scope with requireScope(Scopes.x) at registration (src/http/routes/*.ts), the equivalent of a named-policy attribute; the README lists the scope per endpoint. The rules are named and listable.
verdicts.action: promoted to trap TRP-003 (authorization-enforcement, repository-level must-not-fire); code kept. Caught by TRP-003 in iteration 2

verdicts.message: Changelog looks stale/thin: The changelog this check read carries 2 versioned entries, against a bar of 3. scoreBands.note: C2 docks for 'no named authorization policies' although every route names its scope (TRP-003). Band kept.
M2's top tier wants many more ADRs; the repository records its 3 real decisions plus a Mermaid architecture doc. Band set before the first scan and kept.

P6 does not count package.json version 1.0.0 as a version stamp (on its scaffold-default list), although it matches the CHANGELOG's one release. Version not changed to suit the scanner. final-llm pass at the frozen tag: P6 80 (versioning credited from the git tag v1.0.0, changelog still 'thin') -> in; the iteration-2 'out' was taken before the tag existed.

BND-003 duplicated-code was out in iteration 1 (R10 81) for partly valid reasons; in band at 96 after the fix. Model-judged (two host passes, identical): D19 90, D20 100, D21 100, M4 60 - in band; D22, D24, D25, LA3, LA4 emitted no score. Unscored in the contained pass: D5 (instability/main sequence), D16/D34 (single-author history), D27, S1 (server controls not assessed for TypeScript; a clean S1 abstains), SC1 (never scored), D36 (publishes nothing), P4, P5, P7, P12, PF1, PF2.

observations: A deliberately clean, idiomatic Node.js 22 + TypeScript API (1.1k LoC production, 1.1k test) drew 8 deterministic rows in iteration 1: 5 valid (an untested entry point, four duplicated route/problem blocks, all fixed), 1 false positive (C2 named policies), 2 opinion-not-fact (P6 changelog bar, R10 on parallel accessors). After the fixes only the recorded noise remained, two rows of it caught by traps promoted from it.
The scanner runs the vitest suite itself with v8 coverage (npm ci, then vitest --coverage) in contained mode; per-file coverage findings on TypeScript are real measurements.

The model-judged M4 pass reported 39 'README/code drift' rows that restate README sentences as claims (every configuration default, the licence, the contribution rules); every one holds. M4 still scored 60. This is the dominant noise source on this repository.
Two host --with-llm passes on the same tree produced byte-identical SARIF, which suggests reused model responses rather than determinism; the C# control saw run-to-run M4 variation.
P6 treats package.json version 1.0.0 as a scaffold default, so a genuine first release scores 30.

S1 does not assess server-side controls (helmet headers, HSTS, HTTPS enforcement, zod validation) for TypeScript and abstains on a clean repository: BND-018..020 cannot be scored for a Node service under this scanner version.

Not the instrument, for completeness: GitHub CodeQL raised js/user-controlled-bypass (authentication.ts, the result of a signature verification) and js/missing-rate-limiting (rate limiting is the gateway's job per SECURITY.md); both judged noise in the journal.

Final host pass (2026-10-07, TS sidecar repaired): no new result and no model-judged band moved. The repaired code model adds the D1/D2/D6/D26/D35/AX* cards to the host pass (same values as the contained pass). The only score change, P6 30 -> 80 (BND-032 out -> in), comes from scanning the tagged commit, not from the model.
